writeup.headline: Danaher rates Hold: strong quality and momentum, offset by debt and absolute valuation, four points shy of Buy.
writeup.thesis: Danaher scores 61, a Hold, four points below the Buy threshold. Quality is the main support at 78, with a 58.6% gross margin, 20.4% operating margin, 22.4% FCF margin and diluted share count down 1.0% year on year, and the trend score of 79 reflects a price 16.4% above its 200-day average and shares 22.3 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Growth is middling at 51, with TTM revenue growth of 5.5%, though latest-quarter revenue growth of 8.3% year on year shows growth sped up by 2.7 pp from the previous quarter. Holding the score back are the balance sheet (38, net debt at 3.63 times FCF and cash covering 0.21 of debt) and valuation (42), where absolute levels are high, with P/FCF of 28.8x, EV/EBIT of 35.5x and FCF yield 1.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, while overall the multiples sit near the middle of its own history. News is supportive at 71 after a Q3 beat and a raised full-year adjusted EPS guide of $8.57 to $8.62.
key_risks: Absolute valuation is high (EV/EBIT 35.5x, P/FCF 28.8x), leaving little room for disappointment.
Leverage is meaningful, with net debt at 3.63 times FCF and cash at 0.21 of debt.
Q4 guidance implies only about 3% core growth including the respiratory headwind.
Academic demand remains below historical levels despite sequential improvement.
With the price 3.3% below its 52-week high after a strong run, momentum could fade.
what_would_change: A 4-point score gain would reach Buy, e.g. from sustained acceleration lifting the growth score above 51 or debt reduction improving the balance sheet score of 38.
A pullback in multiples or rising FCF would improve the valuation score of 42 and could tip the rating to Buy.
A fall below 45 (17 points down) would mean Sell, likely requiring a broken trend, guidance cuts and weaker growth together.
